chunks: 1003 - Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who recited aloud where aloud recitation should not be done, or recited quietly where quiet recitation should not be done, he said: “Whichever of the two he does deliberately, he has invalidated his salat (prayer) and repetition is upon him. But if he does that forgetfully, or absentmindedly, or without knowing, then there is nothing upon him, and his salat (prayer) has been completed.”

He said: I said to him, “A man forgot the recitation in the first two rakʿahs, then remembered it in the last two.” He said: “He makes up the recitation, the takbir, and the tasbih that he missed in the first two during the last two, and there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.الْإِخْفَاءُ: quiet or silent recitation in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone recites aloud or silently in the wrong part of salat (prayer) by mistake or forgetfulness?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on mistakes in salat (prayer), especially reciting aloud or silently in the wrong place. It distinguishes between deliberate action, which invalidates the prayer and requires repetition, and mistakes due to forgetfulness, heedlessness, or ignorance, which do not invalidate it. It also explains that missed recitation and related invocations in the first two rakʿahs may be made up in the latter two.
